lessons.title: いった ほうが いいです (itta hō ga ii desu) — you had better
lessons.headword: いった ほうが いいです
lessons.gloss: you had better go — -ta hō ga ii desu for advice, -nai hō ga ii desu for advice against

segments.text: Say, plainly, "I rested" and "I won't drink". (yasunda, nomanai.) Then say "medicine". (kusuri.)

blocks.title: You'll want to know: -た ほうが いいです

segments.text: やすんだ ほうが いいです。 yasunda hō ga ii desu. — "You had better rest."
ほう (hō) is "side, way": "the side of having rested is good". The plain past goes before it even when the advice is about now or later.
くすりを のんだ ほうが いいです。 kusuri o nonda hō ga ii desu. — "You had better take some medicine."
びょういんに いった ほうが いいです。 byōin ni itta hō ga ii desu. — "You had better go to the hospital."

blocks.title: You'll want to know: -ない ほうが いいです

segments.text: Advice against takes the plain "not":
おさけを のまない ほうが いいです。 osake o nomanai hō ga ii desu. — "You had better not drink alcohol."
あぶないから、いかない ほうが いいです。 abunai kara, ikanai hō ga ii desu. — "It is dangerous, so you had better not go."
This is advice. Saying that something must be done needs another form, which comes later.

lessons.title: だから (dakara) — so; that is why

segments.text: Before the new word: say "it is cold, so I won't go". (samui kara, ikimasen.) Then "you had better not go". (ikanai hō ga ii desu.)

blocks.title: You'll want to know: だから

segments.text: だから — dakara — "so", "that is why". It opens a new sentence with the result, after a sentence that gave the reason:
あめが ふっています。 ame ga futte imasu. — "It is raining."
だから、いきません。 dakara, ikimasen. — "So I won't go."
It is plain, the word for a friend; the next lesson gives its polite partner.

だから (dakara) is a native Japanese word (wago), inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese: だ (da), the plain form of です, and から (kara), "because". JMdict lists it as a conjunction, "so; therefore", written in kana (JMdict).

segments.prompt: Say the Japanese for 'so, that is why', to a friend.

segments.text: "So", opening a sentence, to a friend? (だから, dakara.) Which comes first, the reason or だから? (The reason, in the sentence before.)

lessons.title: ですから / それで (desu kara / sore de) — so, and so
lessons.gloss: so, and so — desu kara, the polite dakara, and sore de for what came of it

segments.text: Say "so I won't go", to a friend. (dakara, ikimasen.) Then say "a holiday". (yasumi.)

blocks.title: You'll want to know: ですから

segments.text: To a teacher, in a shop or at work, だから (dakara) becomes ですから (desu kara), with です in place of だ:
あしたは やすみです。 ashita wa yasumi desu. — "Tomorrow is a holiday."
ですから、みせは しまっています。 desu kara, mise wa shimatte imasu. — "So the shop is closed."

blocks.title: You'll want to know: それで

segments.text: それで (sore de) is "and so": it tells what came of something that happened. It looks back at an event, where だから (dakara) and ですから also give advice and decisions.
でんしゃが とまりました。 densha ga tomarimashita. — "The train stopped."
それで、おくれました。 sore de, okuremashita. — "And so I was late."
